PANAWAGAN NG MAMAMAYAN NGAYONG ANIBERSARYO NG EDSA

Progressive groups from various sectors across CALABARZON staged a protest action at Plaza Lacson in Sta. Cruz on Tuesday to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the 1986 People Power Revolution.

The mobilization, spearheaded by Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (BAYAN) Timog Katagalugan, assembled in Mendiola before marching to EDSA to join a broader national mobilization calling for accountability and justice.

data.text:
On 25 February 1986, Corazon Aquino—seen here, second from left, during a Women’s Day protest march in Manila the previous year—was sworn in as the first female president of the Philippines. This marked the end of Ferdinand Marcos’s authoritarian regime, which had been notorious for its corruption and suppression of democratic processes.

Elected in 1965, Marcos had instituted martial law in 1972 and jailed a number of his political opponents. These included Aquino’s husband, Benigno, who was sentenced to death by a military commission, on charges of subversion, murder and possessing illegal firearms. Marcos commuted the death sentence in 1980, allowing the Aquinos to live in exile in the United States. He ended martial law the following year but retained dictatorial control over the government.

Benigno flew back to the Philippines in 1983, intending to campaign in the forthcoming elections that had been promised by the government. Upon disembarking at Manila International Airport, he was shot dead. His killing galvanised opposition against the Marcos regime, which appointed a commission of inquiry that held senior military officers responsible for the assassination. To reassert his mandate amid growing protests, Marcos called a snap presidential election in February 1986. The united opposition nominated Corazon as its candidate.

Although official reports claimed that Marcos had won the election, Aquino and her followers challenged the results, alleging widespread fraud. The military leadership was split among whom to support. Both sets of supporters proclaimed their candidates as having been elected on 25 February, but, at the urging of the US government, Marcos fled the country with his family that same day, later settling in Hawaii. Aquino established a provisional constitution and appointed a commission to draft a final version. The new constitution, which restored the bicameral legislature that Marcos had abolished, was ratified by a landslide margin in a 1987 referendum.

PCO holds press briefing with MMDA (February 25, 2026)

* MMDA General Manager Gen. Nicolas Torre: Kung kailangan niyo po ng responde sa kalsada, sa mga major roads na covered na MMDA, ang number po na tatawagan ay Metrobase 136.

* Torre: Ang aming garantiya riyan, limang minuto, makakarating ang aming mga traffic enforcers kung saan may nangangailangan ng tulong.

* Torre: Kapag may banggaan, hihingiin ang inyong social media account para maipadala ang clip o CCTV footage. Gusto natin within 10 minutes, cleared na ang kalsada.

* Torre: We have sufficient manpower right now.

* Torre: Constant ang aming mga changes regarding traffic schemes.

* Torre: Hindi naman tayo nag-a-AI ng NCAP violations. Nandiyan ang sistema.

* Torre sa inilabas na listahan ni Atty. Baligod: It’s a non-issue right now for me because hindi naman ako ang bida diyan, napakaraming pangalan.

* Usec. Claire Castro: Narinig niyo po ang requirements sa pagkapangulo. Ang sabi [ni PBBM], dapat nakakaintindi ng economics. Ang sabi rin niya, dapat naiintindihan ang tungkol sa inflation. Pati ang paggawa ng trabaho, at ang food supply.

* Castro: Sa mga nangunguna o inuuna ang politika sa ngayon, mag-isip-isip at baka hindi kayo qualified.

* Castro: Si [VP Sara], naitalaga siya bilang secretary ng DepEd, pinagtiwalaan siya ng Pangulo, pero sa bandang huli, aamin pala ang Bise na wala siyang kaalam-alam sa pagiging DepEd secretary.

* Castro: Lahat ng multong ito ni VP Sara noong siya ay DepEd secretary, huwag niyang ipahid kay PBBM.

* Castro: Paulit-ulit na kasinungalingan laban sa Pangulo. Lousy script, hindi pang-award winning. Hindi malinis — alam mo na may kasinungalingan.

* Castro: Sino ba ang nasa likod nito? Siguro dapat malaman ninyo kung sino bang may-ari ng sasakyan na sumundo sa kanila matapos ang presscon. 

* Castro: I believe hindi kayo magugulat. Same people. Nandyan ang NBI, PNP, at DOJ. Obligasyon nilang kasuhan ang mga nagpapakalat ng fake news.

data.text:
Nakatutok ang MMDA Emergency Operations Center (EOC) sa sitwasyon ng trapiko sa paligid ng EDSA People Power Monument para sa "Trillion Peso March 3" kasabay ng paggunita sa ika-40 anibersaryo ng 1986 People Power Revolution ngayong araw.

Sa direktiba ni MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, tinutukan ang sitwasyon sa EDSA at iba pang pangunahing lansangan ng Metro Manila sa pamamagitan ng Closed-Circuit Television (CCTVs) sa MMDA Communications and Command Center. 

Nakadeploy naman ang  972 kawani ng MMDA mula sa Traffic Discipline Office, Road Emergency Group, Public Safety Division, Metro Parkways Clearing Group, at Metrobase, sa pakikipagtulungan sa Philippine National Police, Quezon City government, at iba pang ahensiya ng pamahalaan. 

Kaninang umaga, nagmartsa ang mga miyembro ng Trillion Peso March Movement, ilang religious groups at political leaders, mula sa EDSA Shrine at iba pang lugar sa Metro Manila patungong People Power Monument para sa isang pagtitipon. 

Katuwang din ng MMDA sa monitoring ang mga kinatawan mula sa Department of Transportation-Special Action and Intelligence Committee for Transportation (DOTr-SAICT), Bureau of Fire Protection, National Capital Region Command (NCRCOM) ng Armed Forces of the Philippines at National Intelligence Coordinating Agency (NICA) sa layunin na masiguro ang kaligtasan ng mga lalahok sa aktibidad at ng mga motorista. #mmda #mmdaatyourservice
